subject: Evidence request: egress & microsegmentation controls for Dedicated/Private
messages:
From: Jenna Martin <jenna@acmesec.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Paul Fitzgerald <paul.fitzgerald@enterprise-apps.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence request: Dedicated/Private network segmentation & egress controls

Hi Olga,

We're starting the SIG/SOC2 scoping for Enterprise Apps' procurement review. To complete the network architecture portion we need evidence of how Redwood isolates customer workloads for your Dedicated and Private deployment modes and how outbound traffic is controlled. Specifically: 

- High-level network diagram showing subnets, transit components, and any peering/transit gateways used for Dedicated vs Private.
- A clear statement of where egress is allowed (internet, partner clouds, customer backends) and what controls are enforced (NAT/proxy, firewall rules, TLS inspection).
- Firewall/NACL and security group rule examples for both control plane and data plane.
- Any microsegmentation approach (e.g., host-based, network policies, service mesh) and how it’s applied per-tenant.
- Evidence: sample firewall configs, egress policy matrix, and a sanitized diagram suitable for external review.

Can you provide these by next Tue (2026-07-14)? If some artifacts are considered internal-only, please indicate that and we can coordinate an NDA/secure upload.

Thanks,
Jenna Martin
Senior Assessor, Acme Security Assessments

-----
Jenna Martin
Acme Security Assessments
https://acmesec.com

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Martin <jenna@acmesec.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence request: Dedicated/Private network segmentation & egress controls

Hi Jenna —

Thanks for the checklist. We're on it. Quick notes & proposed delivery: 

- We can produce a sanitized public-facing network diagram for Dedicated and Private showing VPC boundaries, transit gateway, and high-level peering (redwood_network_overview_v3.drawio.pdf).
- For detailed evidence (security group/NACL snippets, NAT/proxy configs) we will provide redacted snippets suitable for auditors (nat-proxy-config.txt, egress_policy_matrix.csv).
- There is a more detailed internal-only VPC peering map (vpc_peering_map_internal.svg) that we prefer to share under a short-term NDA/secure upload — please confirm you have the upload token.
- We'll include a short explainer (isolation-readme.md) that describes our microsegmentation approach: tenant isolation via dedicated routing + per-tenant security groups, combined with host-level process isolation on Dedicated pools.

Proposed timeline: sanitized diagrams + matrix by Tue (2026-07-14) EOD, internal artefacts to follow on secure upload by Thu (2026-07-16).

Cc'ing David to pull firewall/NACL rule examples and Grace to attach the canary test plan for egress monitoring.

Best,
Olga
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood_network_overview_v3.drawio.pdf (sanitized), egress_policy_matrix.csv (summary), nat-proxy-config.txt (sample)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Evidence request: Dedicated/Private network segmentation & egress controls

Olga / Grace —

Dropping in the examples I promised. High level: Dedicated pools get customer-dedicated subnets and per-tenant security groups. Private deployments sit inside customer VPCs with a lightweight control-plane peering model. Egress is blocked by default; allowed egress paths require an explicit approved rule in our egress_policy_matrix.csv.

Attached (sanitized):
- nat-proxy-config.txt — shows NAT Gateway + outbound proxy header insertion and allowlist enforcement.
- egress_policy_matrix.csv — canonical table mapping service -> allowed destinations -> justification -> approval owner.

Notes: we do not perform TLS interception on customer application traffic by default; we rely on egress allowlists and proxy-based domain deny/allow rules. For telemetry we forward logs to our tenant-specific logging buckets (encrypted) and to customer endpoints only when contracted.

-David
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: nat-proxy-config.txt (text, redacted), egress_policy_matrix.csv (csv, redacted)

From: Paul Fitzgerald <paul.fitzgerald@enterprise-apps.com>
To: Jenna Martin <jenna@acmesec.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence request: Dedicated/Private network segmentation & egress controls

Thanks — quick follow-ups from the procurement/security team at Enterprise Apps: 

- Can the sanitized diagram include a legend for connectivity types (VPC peering vs transit gateway vs private link)?
- We need one example of a firewall/security group rule that shows how a control-plane endpoint is restricted (IP ranges, port ranges).
- For SOC2 evidence: can you provide dated logs that show a canary test failing/alerting for an attempted unauthorized egress in the last 90 days? A redacted sample log is fine.

Also, we are happy to accept internal-only artifacts through Acme's secure upload token; Jenna, please confirm.

-Paul
Director, Cloud Platform Procurement
Enterprise Apps Inc.

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Martin <jenna@acmesec.com>, Paul Fitzgerald <paul.fitzgerald@enterprise-apps.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence request: Dedicated/Private network segmentation & egress controls

Paul / Jenna —

Thanks for the clarifying questions. Quick replies: 

- We'll update the sanitized diagram to include a connectivity legend and call out which links are managed by Redwood vs customer-managed. Expect the revised diagram in the shared Drive link below.
- Attached in the secure bundle is a redacted security-group example that shows control-plane restriction to management IP ranges and port 443 only. (See "redwood_network_overview_v3.drawio.pdf" and the secure upload for the SG snippet).
- For the canary evidence: Grace has prepared a redacted alert sample pulled from our canary-run on 2026-05-21 that demonstrates an outbound deny and the associated audit entry. The canaries-test-plan.pdf documents frequency and scope.

We uploaded the sanitized artifacts and redacted samples to our secure collection: https://drive.redwood.example.com/secure/Shared/egress-evidence-2026-07-15. Acme upload token for internal artifacts: https://acme.sharefile.com/request/XYZ-Upload-Token

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min walkthrough next week to step through the diagrams and the test evidence.

Best regards,
Olga Petrov
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
